title: Cohomology on a quasi-compact open commutes with directed colimits of modules (Stacks 01FF, for schemes)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space has the following two properties: (1) the quasi-compact open subsets [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] form a basis of the topology, and (2) the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact. Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ be a system of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), and let $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_{i\in I})$ be a colimit of this system in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ write $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=H^q(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ for the cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] of the open subscheme $U$ with coefficients in the restriction $\mathcal G|_U$ ($W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ for opens $W\subseteq U$), and $H^q(U,h)$ for the map induced by a morphism $h$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then for every quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ and every $q\ge0$: (a) every $x\in H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ is of the form $H^q(U,c_i)(y)$ for some $i\in I$ and $y\in H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$; (b) if $i\in I$ and $y\in H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$ satisfy $H^q(U,c_i)(y)=0$, then $H^q(U,\varphi_{i'i})(y)=0$ for some $i'\ge i$. In other words, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH^q(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ from the directed colimit of the abelian groups $H^q(U,\mathcal F_i)$, whose restriction to the $i$-th term is $H^q(U,c_i)$, is bijective.

proof.text: Convert hBasis by IsTopologicalBasis.exists_subset_of_mem_open and obtain compact binary intersections by IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen. Apply abelianSections_preservesDirectedColimits to the abelian evaluation functor E. The exact, colimit-preserving module forgetful functor T has T composed with E definitionally equal to openModuleSections, so sections of modules preserve I-colimits as well. The preservation instances for T are the proved upstream sheaf-module instances.

proof.text: Induct on n to prove that the right derived functor of openModuleSections in degree n preserves all I-colimits. At zero transport section preservation along rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. At the successor apply preservesColimitsOfShape_rightDerived_succ in the Grothendieck module-sheaf category. Its proof supplies the functorial injective diagram, exact colimit short sequence and connecting-map ladder. It remains only to verify that colimits of injective module diagrams are acyclic for open sections.

proof.text: For a diagram J of injective modules, apply topological_filtered_cohomology to J composed with T in degree n+1. It gives preservation of the canonical colimit by the abelian object-cohomology functor C. Since T preserves the module colimit, C(T(colimit J)) is the colimit of C(T(J_i)). Each latter object is zero by injective_module_abelian_acyclic; IsColimit.isZero_pt therefore proves that C(T(colimit J)) is zero.

source.place: Tag 01FF, lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit; stage-3 route through existing abelian-sheaf and derived-composite tools

proof.text: Use nonempty_cohomologyPresheafFunctor_eval_iso_rightDerived to transport this zero object to derived abelian sections of T(colimit J). The same comparison and injective_module_abelian_acyclic show that T sends every injective module to an E-acyclic abelian sheaf. Apply exists_rightDerived_exact_comp_iso to exact T and left exact E. Its object comparison identifies module-derived open sections with derived abelian sections after T. Transport zero along it, completing the successor premise and the induction.

proof.text: Apply IsColimitOfPreserves to the given cocone c in degree q. Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep gives the first assertion. For a stage element y mapping to zero, compare its image with that of zero at the same stage and use Concrete.isColimit_rep_eq_iff_exists; the resulting two transition arrows have target j, and additivity sends the second zero to zero. In a preorder the first arrow is equal by subsingleton elimination to homOfLE of its underlying inequality, giving the second assertion exactly. These are the concrete filtered-colimit APIs for abelian groups; no antisymmetry or positive-degree restriction is used.
